title: C1035B — Battery junction box (BJB) connector
introduction:
I read this battery junction box reference by matching identity before interpreting function. A familiar-looking connection is like a familiar-looking key: its outline helps, but the label still deserves your attention.

Begin with the connector identification table. The harness heading leads to the drawing and its associated Fpn entry; the drawing’s cavity label then selects the matching Cavity row in the assignment table. Read across for the circuit identity, wire description, function and terminal identification. Keep the starter-preference wording attached to the Function entry. It describes a preference, not a complete starter wiring route or permission to change the connection.

This page supports reading the connection map. Access, disconnection, wire selection, probing and replacement require the applicable service information. The physical viewing side, gauge convention and meanings of Size and Used are unspecified; retain those entries without converting them into dimensions, ratings or test criteria.

edits.why: I use the rounded end, offset projecting tab and barrel outline as landmarks for this drawing. The cavity label connects those visual details to the assignment table. They help distinguish the illustrated connection without establishing an access route, physical viewing side or removal method.

Follow the cavity match across the row rather than choosing a connection by wire appearance alone. The Function entry retains both its fuse designation and its starter preference. That describes the assigned role; it does not establish the downstream route, the condition of the fuse or the cause of a starting complaint.
